GOOD TO KNOW

Calling hours worldwide: every number is placed in its own time zone, also in countries with several (United States, Canada, Mexico, Brazil, Russia, Australia and more), from its area code, or from the customer's postal code or state where known. A number that may be in two zones is only called when it is inside hours in both. Existing numbers are placed by themselves over the first few minutes after the update.

Paused campaigns no longer pause again the moment they are resumed: after an automatic pause for dropped calls, the pause is judged on calls answered since the resume, and the campaign restarts cautiously.

Manual calls go to a queue the agent works (a queue whose skills they have, the one they last worked in first). Before, every manual call without a campaign went to the same queue, whoever dialled it.

Email auto-replies: an out-of-hours reply is no longer skipped because the customer had just received a ticket acknowledgement. A rule's "once per sender" counts only that rule's own earlier replies.

Calls left open after the customer hung up are closed by themselves after two minutes, so they no longer sit in Live calls as waiting.

Mailboxes with a call flow: a step that asks only with a recording (which an email or chat cannot hear) now hands the conversation to people at once, instead of holding it for a day waiting for a reply.

AI agents: when the voice server is busy it is asked again a moment later, at most four lines are asked of it at once, and a voice that does not start a line within 12 seconds hands the caller to a person.

FOR AGENTS

Outcome keys: in wrap-up, the number keys 1 to 9 and 0 choose the outcomes in the order shown; an outcome set can also let a key hang up and choose in one go.

Dial next: on manual and preview campaigns, take the next lead from the list as a preview, then Dial or Skip with a reason and a time to call again. An optional countdown dials by itself.

Park: Park puts the customer on hold music while you check something; Pick up brings them back.

Pause after a call: a campaign or your profile can pause you after each call, and "Pause after this call" does it once. Some campaigns ask for a pause reason before you go available again.

When the customer hangs up first, the call bar says so in red.

New call stays on the desk while you hold an email, chat or ticket; only a call in hand or ringing hides it.

The desk's phone picks up its calls within a couple of seconds on any network. On some networks (a VPN or a strict firewall) it rang until the platform gave up, so outbound calls never reached the customer and inbound calls never reached the agent.

FOR SUPERVISORS

Real-time view: a new tab on the Live monitor with each campaign's dial level, drop rate, calls, leads and lines in use, calls waiting oldest first, and every agent coloured by state with a timer (ready, on a call, parked, customer hung up, wrap-up, paused with the reason), red past each limit, with listen, whisper and join.

Pacing in plain words: the reasons a campaign is holding back ("held below its dial level by the campaign's most calls at once") are written out on the Pacing panel and the Live monitor.

Abandoned calls report: per campaign and per drop rate group, per day and over the regulator's period, with breaches highlighted, and an alert when a campaign nears its limit.

Supervisors start, pause, resume and stop campaigns; changing a running campaign's speed stays with campaign managers.

FOR ADMINISTRATORS

Recorded messages: the voicemail drop, the answering-machine message, the abandoned-call message and the recording announcement can each be a recording from your prompts, typed text, or a recording named per lead.
